description: ASTROENGINEERS is a team passionate about engineering, space exploration, and innovation. We aim to transform creative ideas into practical solutions using technology, scientific research, and teamwork. We welcome curious minds who love solving problems and exploring new possibilities. We are looking for motivated members with skills in programming, AI, data analysis, engineering, astronomy, and UI/UX design.
summary:
ARTEMIS-X Navigator is an interactive 3D and 2D digital twin engineered to optimize lunar south pole landing missions using real NASA datasets (LRO, LOLA, and Diviner). Mission planners input engineering constraints—such as minimum solar illumination and maximum safe terrain slope—allowing the dynamic solver to automatically pinpoint optimal landing coordinates in real time.

The platform features three synchronized views: a 3D Orbital Twin, an interactive 2D Polar Map with live rotating solar shadows across the 29.5-day lunar cycle, and a Thermal & Elevation spectrum tracking temperatures from -35°C down to -230°C. It also includes a live trade-off table benchmarking target sites against actual historical landings (Chandrayaan-3 and IM-1 Odysseus), paired with an integrated AI Mission Copilot that analyzes telemetry and controls navigation via natural language.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

ARTEMIS-X Navigator is an interactive 3D and 2D digital twin engineered to optimize lunar south pole landing missions. Integrating real NASA datasets—including LRO orbital imagery, LOLA terrain elevation, and Diviner thermal profiles—the platform allows mission planners to input custom engineering constraints (minimum solar illumination percentage, maximum safe terrain slope, and Earth communication line-of-sight). Our dynamic solver immediately calculates and pins the optimal landing coordinates (Latitude, Longitude, and Lunar XYZ) across three synchronized views: a 3D Orbital Twin showing tidal locking, an interactive 2D Polar Map with real-time rotating solar shadows across the 29.5-day lunar cycle, and a Thermal & Elevation spectrum tracking temperatures from -35°C down to -230°C.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

By transforming complex orbital mechanics and multi-layered NASA telemetry into an intuitive decision engine, ARTEMIS-X Navigator significantly reduces mission landing risks. It prevents landers from touching down on steep crater walls or freezing inside Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSR) while keeping them close to water-ice deposits and continuous solar power—directly supporting sustainable human exploration under the Artemis program.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) for real-time physics calculations and polar stereographic projections.

- Visualization & UI Libraries: Three.js (WebGL) for 3D rendering, HTML5 2D Canvas & SVG for solar shadow sweeps and thermal overlays, Chart.js for 29.5-day telemetry curves, and Tailwind CSS.

- Data Sources: NASA LRO, LOLA DEM, Diviner Lunar Radiometer, NASA SVS, and DSN/LunaNet parameters.

- Development Tools: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) and GitHub.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

Unlike static landing maps, our solution introduces real-time dynamic benchmarking against actual historical missions (Chandrayaan-3 and IM-1 Odysseus) alongside an integrated AI Mission Copilot that responds to natural language commands. Our team carefully considered extreme low-angle solar incidence at the South Pole, cryogenic thermal survival thresholds, terrain slope safety limits, and Earth libration communication windows.
